Neighbor Dissimilarity Between Two Graphs

Source: R/neighbor-dissimilarity.R
neighbor_dissimilarity.Rd

Compare how many neighbors each pair of observations shares in two directed nearest-neighbor graphs on the same observations.

Usage

neighbor_dissimilarity(nn_in, nn_out, k = 15, ret_extra = FALSE)

Arguments

nn_in, nn_out

Reference and output graphs with the same rows in the same order. Supply lists with a nearest-first idx matrix as returned by nn_preservation(). Distances are optional. Self indices are stripped.

k

Number of non-self neighbors to use from each row.

ret_extra

Return the separate scores for gains and losses and the row pairs whose shared-neighbor counts changed?

Value

A scalar, with smaller values indicating closer shared-neighbor structure. With ret_extra = TRUE, a list containing nd, gain and loss (the nonnegative directional norms), and pairs. The data frame contains one row per changed unordered pair (i < j), with one-based row positions and neighbor counts shared_in and shared_out.

Details

For each graph, divide the number of shared neighbors of each pair by k. Subtract the reference fractions from the output fractions. Compute the Frobenius norms of the positive and negative parts of this difference matrix. The larger norm is Neighbor Dissimilarity (ND). Both orders of each pair enter the norms. Zero means all shared counts agree, which can happen even when neighbor identities change.

ND depends on graph size and k. Compare embeddings on the same rows and at the same k.

Scaling

Each input graph needs only k neighbors per row, but the sparse matrix product represents every pair of rows sharing a neighbor. One neighbor listed by all N rows creates N * (N - 1) / 2 unordered pairs. Even the scalar score can therefore need quadratic memory. ret_extra = TRUE also returns a table of changed pairs. The calculation uses the Matrix package.

References

Fujiwara, T., Kuo, Y.-H., Ynnerman, A., and Ma, K.-L. (2023). Feature Learning for Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction toward Maximal Extraction of Hidden Patterns, equation 3. https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.13891 The authors implement the graph comparison in FEALM. Quadra also reports which observation pairs gained or lost shared neighbors.

See also

mutual_neighbor_correlation(), nn_preservation()

Examples

x <- as.matrix(iris[, -5])
g <- nn_preservation(x, prcomp(x)$x[, 1:2], k = 5,
                     nn_method_in = "brute", ret_extra = TRUE)
neighbor_dissimilarity(g$nn_in, g$nn_out, k = 5)
#> [1] 9.887366
